GenerateMonsters.maps_to: Encounter(monster_classes=[GremlinMerc]).create_monsters (base Encounter, monsters/base.py); the two spawns are SurprisePower.on_death (powers.py), not GenerateMonsters
GenerateMonsters.rationale: C# GremlinMercNormal.cs:48-51 returns a SINGLE-element list, `(GremlinMerc.ToMutable(), "merc")` -- zero RNG draws. CalculateGoldProportion.maps_to: no sim counterpart at any call site
CalculateGoldProportion.rationale:
CLOSED 2026-08-03 (gap-fix pass). `EncounterModel.CalculateGoldProportion` is ported on the `Encounter` base (`1 - escaped creatures / DISTINCT spawned monster models`, the two different shapes the C# uses) and overridden by a new `GremlinMercEncounter` with all THREE arms of GremlinMercNormal.cs:58-69 — 1.0 / 0.5 (fled, nothing stolen) / 0.0 (fled with stolen gold); the queue's recipe named only the 0.0 one. `driver._run_combat` and `conformance.runner` now compute it off the finished combat, as `CombatRoom.OnCombatEnded` does, and pass it to `generate_combat_rewards`, whose `gold_proportion` plumbing already scaled the MONSTER range. `GoldWasStolen` is read as `combat.gold_stolen > 0` rather than stored on the Encounter: these are module-level singletons shared by every combat, and both the Merc's ThieveryPower and the Fat Gremlin's HeistPower are cleared by the death and the escape before rewards generate. Executed: `py audit/tools/encounter_probes_e7.py gremlin-gold` now prints reward-screen gold 0; regression tests in test/test_underdocks.py::TestGremlinMercGoldProportion.

WHAT THE GAP SAID: GremlinMercNormal.CalculateGoldProportion (GremlinMercNormal.cs:58-69) overrides EncounterModel's base formula: if no Fat Gremlin escaped, gold proportion is 1.0 (normal); if one escaped and NO gold was stolen this combat, 0.5; if one escaped AND gold WAS stolen (GoldWasStolen, set by SurprisePower.AfterDeath whenever the Merc's ThieveryPower total was > 0), 0.0 -- the room's Monster gold reward (10-20) is entirely withheld. `EncounterModel.CalculateGoldProportion`'s own BASE formula (`1 - EscapedCreatures.Count / SpawnedEnemies.Count`, EncounterModel.cs:373-376) is not ported anywhere in sts2_rl either -- `grep -rn CalculateGoldProportion|gold_proportion sts2_rl/` finds only `rewards.generate_combat_rewards`'s and `RunState.generate_combat_rewards`'s unused `gold_proportion: float = 1.0` kwarg (rewards.py:860, run.py:1725) -- and the sole production call site, `driver.py`'s `_run_combat` (driver.py:505-525), calls `run.generate_combat_rewards(room_type, encounter=encounter)` with NO `gold_proportion` argument, so it is always 1.0 regardless of what happened in the fight. EXECUTED: `py audit/tools/encounter_probes_e7.py gremlin-gold` reproduces test_underdocks.py::TestGremlinMercThievery.test_fled_fat_gremlin_keeps_gold_lost's own setup (Fat Gremlin escapes after the Merc steals 20 gold) one step further into the reward screen: `run.generate_combat_rewards(RoomType.MONSTER, encounter=GREMLIN_MERC_NORMAL)` returns `rewards.gold == 17` where the game's override computes proportion 0.0 and withholds the ENTIRE Monster gold reward. Directly reachable in ordinary Ironclad play: any Underdocks Gremlin Merc fight where the Merc gets at least one attack in before dying and the Fat Gremlin is not killed before its FLEE_MOVE turn. Proposed mechanism id: `encounter/_gold_proportion` (shared -- the missing BASE formula and the missing driver-side threading affect any encounter with an escaping creature, not only this one; Thieving Hopper, hive act, is the other real case and is outside this batch's unit list). `seam/rewards.json` has ZERO recorded steps today (`json.load(...)['steps'] == []`) -- this mechanism has no seam coverage at all; it surfaces here for the first time. `audit/records/monster/fat_gremlin.json`'s own guard ('The gold payout itself belongs to the encounter/rewards tier, not to this record') explicitly defers this exact question to this record.

ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.maps_to: n/a -- Encounter has no hook-listener interface
ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.rationale: `EncounterModel.ShouldReceiveCombatHooks => false` (EncounterModel.cs:39), not overridden by this unit. The sim's `Encounter` (monsters/base.py) is a plain dataclass with no `on_*`/hook-listener interface at all -- it is never registered with `HookSystem` (grep `hooks.register` across sts2_rl/: only `Creature.__init__`/`Monster.__init__` call it) -- so it architecturally cannot receive a combat hook, matching the false default by construction rather than by an explicit flag. Faithful.

guards.what: G1: the slot LABEL GenerateMonsters/SurprisePower.AfterDeath attach ('merc'/'sneaky'/'fat') is dropped on the sim side
guards.issue: C# attaches a non-null SlotName to all three creatures in this encounter (GremlinMercNormal.cs:12-16's slot constants; GenerateMonsters passes "merc"; SurprisePower.cs:23-24 passes "sneaky"/"fat"). The sim's `GREMLIN_MERC_NORMAL` sets no `monster_slots`, and `SurprisePower.on_death` (powers.py) calls `CreatureCmd.add` with no `slot_name=` for either spawn -- all three `Creature.slot_name`s stay `None`. DORMANT: `GremlinMercNormal` does not override `Slots` (the named row), inheriting EncounterModel's EMPTY default, so `CombatState.SortEnemiesBySlotName`'s comparator (`Encounter.Slots.IndexOf(SlotName)`) returns -1 for every creature in this encounter regardless of its SlotName string (CombatState.cs:495-501) -- the sort the C# still triggers (CombatManager.cs:847-851, `if (creature.SlotName != null) SortEnemiesBySlotName()`) is a no-op on the game side too, and `grep -rn SlotName src/` finds no OTHER reader that applies to GremlinMerc/SneakyGremlin/FatGremlin (PhantasmalGardener's is a cosmetic skin pick and its own gameplay conditional reads the string directly, not via this encounter; Ovicopter/Fabricator/Myte/Exoskeleton/Wriggler's readers are their own encounters' mechanisms). EXECUTED: `py audit/tools/encounter_probes_e7.py gremlin-slot` -- `GREMLIN_MERC_NORMAL.slots == ()`, all three `Creature.slot_name is None`, and `combat.sort_enemies_by_slot_name` (combat.py:1317-1337) itself early-returns whenever `encounter.slots` is empty, so the dropped labels have no reachable observer in this build on either side. This looks isolated to GremlinMerc/Surprise rather than a systemic pattern: sibling spawners in other acts thread `slot_name` correctly (`monsters/glory/fabricator.py:217`, `monsters/hive/ovicopter.py:158` both pass `slot_name=` to `CreatureCmd.add`). Proposed mechanism id: `encounter/gremlin_merc/g1`.

guards.what: Gold reward ladder (MinGoldReward/MaxGoldReward, inherited from EncounterModel -- not overridden by this unit)
guards.rationale: EncounterModel.cs:64-100: RoomType.Monster -> 10-20, Elite -> 35-45, Boss -> 100-100 (both bounds equal), times AscensionHelper.PovertyAscensionGoldMultiplier under Poverty. sts2_rl/rewards.py:170-174's `GOLD_REWARD_RANGES` pins the identical non-ascension triple `{MONSTER: (10, 20), ELITE: (35, 45), BOSS: (100, 100)}`; rewards.py's own module docstring (line 32) states ascension/Poverty scaling is out of scope, matching this audit's own scope line (`PROMPT.md` Scope section: 'Ascension values: out of scope'). This unit passes no `min_gold`/`max_gold` override to its sim `Encounter`, so `generate_combat_rewards` (rewards.py:885-887) falls through to the room-type default range -- matching the C#'s own inheritance of the base ladder.

guards.what: Per-encounter Rng independence (EncounterModel.cs:41-49's own doc comment: the encounter's Rng is independent of the run's centralized Rng, safe because its state need not survive past the encounter)
guards.rationale: Stream IDENTITY (which Rng object, how it is seeded) is `seam/rng_streams`'s mechanism, not this record's -- cited, not re-verdicted, per PROMPT.md rule 3 and this batch's brief. What IS this record's to check: does the sim's draw actually land on that independent per-encounter Rng rather than a shared/run-level one? `sts2_rl/run.py:1609-1613`'s `create_combat` builds `encounter_selection_rng` via `make_encounter_rng(seed, total_floor, encounter.entry)` (rng.py, verdicted faithful by seam/rng_streams step 21) whenever `self.rng_set is not None` (parity mode -- string- seeded runs, the conformance/replay path) and threads it into `CombatState`/`Encounter.create_monsters` as `selection_rng` (combat.py:222-223). In that mode the draw this record verdicts lands on the correct independent stream. When `rng_set is None` (legacy mode -- `run.py:1609`'s own comment: 'Legacy runs pass None and keep their random.Random composition draws', the RL-training path: `grep -n rng_set sts2_rl/run_env.py` returns zero hits, so training never sets it), `selection_rng` is None and the draw falls back to the shared legacy `random.Random` -- the game's independence guarantee is not honoured in that mode. This is the SAME sim-wide, already-documented parity-vs-legacy split every other RNG consumer in this codebase carries (seam/rng_streams's own G2-adjacent discussion of `CombatRng`'s legacy fallback), not a defect specific to this encounter, and it does not affect the conformance/replay path this campaign's own symptom (89U21BV1TZ) is measured against. Checked per this batch's brief instruction; not filed as a new gap.
